title.value: On Dynamic Programming Decompositions of Static Risk Measures in Markov Decision Processes
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: On Dynamic Programming Decompositions of Static Risk Measures in Markov Decision Processes

extractions.description: The paper addresses the challenges of optimizing risk-averse objectives in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), with a focus on static risk measures such as Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR), Entropic-Value-at-Risk (EVaR), and Value-at-Risk (VaR). It critiques existing dynamic programming decompositions and proposes new solutions for VaR.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on mathematical and theoretical advancements in optimization for risk-averse objectives in decision-making processes without a specific link to climate or ecological themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our findings are significant because risk-averse algorithms are used in high-stakes environments, making their correctness much more critical.

primary_category.justification: There is no direct mention or focus on climate or ecologically-related sustainable development within the content of this paper.
primary_category.quote: Our findings are significant because risk-averse algorithms are used in high-stakes environments, making their correctness much more critical.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address secondary climate or ecological themes as it is focused on optimization and risk measures in a mathematical context.
secondary_categories.quote: This paper shows that a popular decomposition approach to solving MDPs with CVaR and EVaR objectives is suboptimal.

primary_sub_category.quote: Dynamic programming, the linchpin of most RL algorithms, cannot be used directly to optimize a risk measure like VaR or CVaR in MDPs.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: Risk-averse reinforcement learning (RL) seeks to provide a risk-averse policy for high-stakes real-world decision problems.

applications.justification: The paper's methodology and findings have applications in optimizing decisions where risk is a significant factor, such as autonomous driving and investment.
applications.quote: These high-stake domains include autonomous driving, robot collision avoidance, liver transplant timing, HIV treatment, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and investment liquidation, to name a few.
